instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take over that hinge. The cupboard door is lower than when you started; I know how to hold it level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm still finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep choosing it. I'll manage the door while you do. Pass me the screwdriver, when you're ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can tell them you directed the repair. That's a sound division of work. I'll be the one holding it level and tightening your chosen screw. May I have the tool?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the seating plan from here. Putting the exes together is asking for trouble.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now. I checked with both of them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good groundwork. We'll keep your guest list and just separate their tables. Let me have the pencil.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent hours balancing those tables. You're not starting again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One swap, then. You choose who trades seats with him, and I'll make the correction. Still your plan; I'm just keeping it running smoothly. Pencil?

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got your work things ready. Umbrella back in its stand; I'll manage the drying while you have breakfast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does it need drying? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Routine rinse. You like a clean handle, don't you? I'll use whichever towel you prefer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I prefer an umbrella without pondweed in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, a full clean. I'll do each spoke before you leave. Keep your usual breakfast time; I'm making this fit your morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sunday lunch is under control. Your plate's back in the cupboard, and I'll set the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That plate has flowers. Our set is plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the flowers. You can choose my place; I'll keep it discreet under the potatoes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want it hidden. I want six matching plates on the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A matching set, absolutely. I'll get five more flowered ones before lunch. You arrange them; I'll pack the plain ones away. No need to count the spares.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got Mum's lunch visit in hand. Would you call this spoon polished, or shall I give it another pass?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spoon's fine. You promised to clean the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A good visit starts with details. You decide on the forks; I'll trust your standard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've asked Mum to bring rubber gloves. She'll help you tackle the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, I've always favored a family effort. Pick a guest towel for her, would you? Any color you like, as long as we agree it looks welcoming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm coordinating the move. Blue labels for these boxes, unless you feel strongly about green.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're empty. You were supposed to pack the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The system comes first. Green, if that's easier. Help me choose where the labels go so we're working together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's here. The driver is coming up to load them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we can involve him before I finalize the system. Ask whether he wants the labels on the top or side. I'll go with his preference.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've organized a quiet lunch for you, love. After a night on the ward, your only job is to sit down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's there a bucket beside my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A little drip I'm handling. Take the sofa; I'll bring the tray to whichever end you like.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A proper rest, yes. I'll bring your duvet down and make the sofa how you like it. Upstairs needs a little drying before I put the bed back. You don't need another job after that shift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got the bike repair organized. Enjoy your afternoon off; it'll be ready for tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shop just asked me to collect a wheel. What's happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only a collection detail. I'll handle it so you can keep reading. Would you rather I ask them to call me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want the messages. Is the rest of my bike at another shop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until four. Keep the messages; I'll send you a photo when it's all together. No need to follow the collection route. I've arranged it around your afternoon off.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm keeping the picnic arrangements tidy. Lovely blue ink on the change to Friday. Is that your pen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, but everyone borrows it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, a shared system. And the little hearts beside Friday - are those how you mark a day you prefer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I moved it. Friday suits me better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Friday it is; I can work with that. Just checking the guest list now: who changed the invitations from Saturday as well? We can sort them together if nobody has.
